title: Nonsquare tangent-conic transition and good coordinates
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a commutative normal Nagata local domain of dimension $2$ defining a rational singularity [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], [def-per-rational-surface-singularity]. Suppose its maximal-ideal-adic completion is normal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $A$ is not regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], and $A$ is Gorenstein, meaning that its injective dimension as an $A$-module is finite. Put $X=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Choose minimal generators $x_1,x_2,x_3$ of $\mathfrak m$ and a nonzero homogeneous quadratic polynomial $q\in k[t_1,t_2,t_3]$ such that $t_i\mapsto x_i\bmod\mathfrak m^2$ induces $k[t_1,t_2,t_3]/(q)\cong\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}A$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Assume $q$ is not a nonzero scalar times the square of a linear polynomial. Then $X$ has at most one singular point. If it has one, say $p$, it is closed and $k$-rational, and the tangent quadratic polynomial of $\mathcal O_{X,p}$ is again not a scalar times a square. There exists a minimal generator $u\in\mathfrak m$ with the following property: choose $v,w$ completing $u$ to a minimal generating set, and express the tangent quadratic polynomial in the corresponding variables $(U,V,W)$; its restriction to $U=0$ is not a scalar times a square of a linear polynomial (the scalar is allowed to be zero). Call this property good. For every good $u$, $p$ lies in the $u$-chart, $u$ generates the ideal of the exceptional divisor in $\mathcal O_{X,p}$, and the image of $u$ is good in $\mathcal O_{X,p}$. Goodness is independent of the generators $v,w$ completing $u$.
